text:
Lara (support): FYI we got a flagged escalation from a customer — their conversational UI is suddenly much more repetitive and "calm" after yesterday's rollout. They say replies feel deterministic.
Maria (cust-succ): Customer says it started after 03:00 UTC yesterday, matches our canary window. They attached a transcript showing shorter, less varied completions.
Lara (support): Pasting their minimal repro: they call /v1/chat/completions without temperature/top_p explicitly set (using default). Example from their client:```curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/chat/completions -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"model":"gpt-open-2","messages":[{"role":"system","content":"You are a helpful assistant."},{"role":"user","content":"Summarize the meeting notes."}]}'```
Jordan (eng-runtime): @Lara thanks. Our rollout did flip the global default sampling profile under flag sampling_defaults_v2 — we intended to lower hallucination risk by setting default temperature=0.2 and top_p=0.6 for some model classes. That would make outputs less stochastic (more deterministic).
Alex (infra): Can we confirm which tenants saw the new default? The rollout targeted hosted API and dedicated with default config inheritance. Looking at rollout-service logs:```
[2026-03-15T03:05:12Z] rollout sampling_defaults_v2 -> traffic: 100% hosted, 30% dedicated
```
Jordan (eng-runtime): Verified. The config was gated by model_family=="gpt-open" which matches the customer's model.
Maria (cust-succ): Customer expects behavior change to be opt-in not opt-out. They relied on higher variance for creative features. This is a user-facing regression.
Lara (support): Customer asked: how do they restore previous randomness immediately?
Jordan (eng-runtime): Immediate workaround: set explicit sampling params in the request body: {"temperature":0.9,"top_p":0.95}. I'll paste an example:```json
{"model":"gpt-open-2","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Write a playful short story."}],"temperature":0.9,"top_p":0.95}
```
Lara (support): I sent that to the customer. They also asked for a rollback.
Alex (infra): Ops-SRE, do we have a quick rollback plan for sampling_defaults_v2?
Ops-SRE: We can revert the rollout flag to previous profile. Risk: it will affect many tenants instantly. We need approval from Product/CS.
Maria (cust-succ): I'll coordinate with the customer on scope and timeframe; they want a tenant-level override if possible. Can we expose per-API-key default overrides?
Jordan (eng-runtime): Per-API-key override exists in Dedicated but for hosted customers defaults inherit from global profile. Short term: we can push a scoped flag to exclude api_key X from sampling_defaults_v2. Need ID.
Lara (support): Customer API key: rk_cust_4F2. Can you scope exclude?
Jordan (eng-runtime): I'll create a targeted exclusion rule and deploy it to the rollout service. ETA ~20m.
eng-runtime-bot: [deployment] rollout-rule-create sampling_defaults_v2_exclude_rk_cust_4F2 by Jordan — queued (id: rr-8812).
Alex (infra): Reminder: add a test that verifies omitted sampling params fall back to the pre-rollout baseline for excluded tenants.
Jordan (eng-runtime): Will do. I'll also add a telemetry flag to surface default-sampling-changes in the console so CS can see which customers are affected next time.
Lara (support): Customer replied: tried explicit temp/top_p, that restored diversity. Happy to wait for the temporary exclusion while Product reviews.
Maria (cust-succ): Opening an internal escalation ticket for policy: defaults that affect output characteristics must go through CS sign-off for hosted users.
Lara (support): Thanks team. I'll keep the customer updated and close once exclusion is live and they confirm.
Ops-SRE: exclusion rule deployed to rollout-service at 1815001420.
Lara (support): Customer confirmed at 1815001448 — behavior back to previous variability. Marking resolved for now. :white_check_mark:
